title: Overload thresholds + hysteresis (working notes)
content:
Last updated: 2026-01-12 (Rafael)

Purpose
- Working notes for proposed breaker thresholds + hysteresis parameters for Hosted API overload protection.
- This is not final policy; goal is to converge on safe defaults per (region, model class, tier) for canary + early rollout.

Where this doc fits
- ADR-0148 defines the state model (closed/open/half-open) and the requirement for hysteresis/cooldowns.
- This doc proposes concrete numbers and per-region adjustments based on recent incidents and canary measurements.
- Error mapping (429/503 + Retry-After + Redwood codes) is ADR-0147.

Owner / review
- Owner: Rafael Mendes (SRE)
- Reviewers: Christine Wong (breaker impl), Mina Haddad (routing), Ravi Menon (capacity signals), Aisha Bello (dashboards)

---

0) Quick glossary / assumptions
- Tier: customer tier classification used for fairness + admission decisions at edge.
  - Tier 0 = internal/system; Tier 1 = enterprise/paid high priority; Tier 2 = standard paid; Tier 3 = free/trial.
- Model class (rough):
  - S = small / fast (e.g., <= ~15B equivalent)
  - M = medium
  - L = large (highest cost, most sensitive to queueing)
- Regions: us-east, us-west, eu-central, ap-southeast (note: names match current hosted capacity partitions).
- Signals (inputs):
  - gpu_pool_util = normalized utilization for the pool (includes scheduling saturation; not raw GPU %)
  - queue_depth = outstanding requests at routing/runtime boundary
  - queue_wait_p99 = p99 time waiting before runtime admission
  - ttft_p99 = p99 time-to-first-token (streaming)
  - e2e_latency_p99 = p99 end-to-end latency (non-streaming)
  - runtime_mem_pressure = normalized (0-1) KV-cache/memory pressure score

Key design bias
- Prefer shedding earlier and deterministically (edge/gateway) when we have strong overload confidence.
- Avoid breaker flapping: open quickly when clearly overloaded, close slowly.

---

1) Incidents / data points informing defaults
(Links in the header; summarizing here so we keep our biases explicit.)

- SUP-3921 / Slack incident thread 1720861145: queue blowup + 503 timeouts; control plane became sluggish due to retry storm.
  - Observation: late shedding at runtime did not prevent tail collapse. Clients interpreted timeouts as retryable with no guidance.

- SUP-3928: mixed 500/502/503 responses during burst; customers couldn’t distinguish overload vs internal failure.
  - Observation: inconsistent mapping created aggressive client retries.

- SUP-3974: after initial rollout, customer saw “unexpected 429s”; root cause was retry loop w/o jitter.
  - Observation: even correct shedding needs explicit Retry-After and SDK guidance.

- Canary notes (us-east, 2 models): breaker flapping bug uncovered → fixed in pr-18519.
  - Observation: close conditions were too eager; needed a longer cooldown + “below threshold for N windows” rule.

---

2) Proposed baseline thresholds (v0)
These are intended as defaults for Hosted; Dedicated will likely have different guardrails (see section 6).

2.1 Edge/Gateway admission control (early shed)
Goal: shed at the edge when the routing breaker is open or when we have high confidence that a particular (region, model class, tier) is in overload.

Inputs (available at gateway):
- breaker_state (from routing)
- per-route shed budget (config)
- request type: streaming vs non-streaming; context length bucket (short/medium/long)

Proposed gateway behavior (not a full policy matrix):
- If breaker_state == OPEN for (model, region, tier):
  - return 503 with Redwood overload code (see ADR-0147) + Retry-After.
  - Retry-After defaults:
    - OPEN due to capacity saturation: 2s
    - OPEN due to mem pressure / OOM risk: 5s
    - OPEN due to control plane protection (routing degraded): 1s
- If breaker_state == HALF_OPEN:
  - allow a small probe fraction (see 3.3) and shed the rest with 503 + Retry-After: 1s

Notes
- We should not return 429 unless the reason is “client/request admission limited” (tier quota / fairness / explicit admission cap). Using 503 for “server is overloaded; try later” is more semantically correct for many clients.
- For OpenAI-compat endpoints: map to consistent error body while preserving HTTP semantics. (See pr-18433 and pr-188.)

2.2 Routing/control-plane circuit breaker open conditions
Unit of breaker: (region, model, tier) — implemented as (region, model_group, tier) initially for cardinality.

Proposed OPEN triggers (any one sustained):
A) Saturation-based
- gpu_pool_util > 0.92 for 60s (rolling window)
  - Rationale: above ~0.9 the queueing slope becomes steep; small spikes cause large tail latency.

B) Queue-based
- queue_depth > Q_max for 30s
  - Q_max default by model class:
    - S: 200
    - M: 120
    - L: 60
  - Q_max should be scaled by provisioned concurrency; above is for current “typical” pool sizes (needs normalization work; see open questions).

C) Wait-time based
- queue_wait_p99 > 1.25s for 90s
  - Rationale: when wait exceeds ~1s, TTFT and E2E p99 explode and customers time out.

D) Runtime mem pressure based (hard protection)
- runtime_mem_pressure > 0.85 for 30s
  - Rationale: KV-cache thrash leads to cascading latency + risk of OOM; open fast.

2.3 Routing breaker close conditions (hysteresis)
Breaker transitions from OPEN → HALF_OPEN only when “healthy enough” for long enough.

Proposed OPEN → HALF_OPEN conditions (all must hold):
- cool_down_elapsed >= 120s (minimum open time)
- gpu_pool_util < 0.80 for 120s
- queue_depth < 0.50 * Q_max for 120s
- runtime_mem_pressure < 0.70 for 120s

Proposed HALF_OPEN → CLOSED conditions:
- probe_success_rate >= 0.98 over 2 minutes (see 3.3 for what success means)
- probe_ttft_p99 < TTFT_close_target (streaming) OR probe_e2e_p99 < E2E_close_target (non-streaming)
  - TTFT_close_target: 900ms
  - E2E_close_target: 2.0s

Proposed HALF_OPEN → OPEN (re-open) conditions:
- any OPEN trigger reappears for >= 30s OR
- probe_success_rate < 0.95 over 60s

---

3) Hysteresis parameters (v0)
These values exist to prevent flapping (and are consistent with pr-18519 adjustments).

3.1 Windowing
- All metrics used for transition decisions should be computed on aligned rolling windows.
  - util window: 30s rollup, evaluated every 10s
  - queue_depth window: 10s rollup, evaluated every 10s
  - p99 windows: 60s rollup, evaluated every 30s

3.2 Cooldowns
- min_open_duration: 120s (default)
- min_half_open_duration: 120s before eligible to close
- min_closed_duration (optional): 60s before eligible to open again based on p99 alone (util/mem can still open immediately)

3.3 Half-open probing
Mechanics (proposal):
- In HALF_OPEN, allow a capped number of requests through per (region, model_group, tier) while shedding the remainder.
- Probe cap:
  - max_probe_rps = 2 rps (S), 1 rps (M), 0.5 rps (L)
  - OR max_probe_fraction = 1% of recent admitted traffic (whichever is larger), bounded above by 5%.

Define probe “success”
- HTTP 2xx/3xx responses.
- Exclude:
  - client cancellations
  - explicit load-shed errors returned by runtime due to downstream guardrails
- For streaming: success must also include “stream started” (TTFT <= 2.0s) to avoid considering late-start streams as healthy.

---

4) Runtime/data-plane shed thresholds (guardrails)
Runtime shedding is the last line of defense; it must be deterministic and reason-coded.

4.1 Bounded queue at runtime scheduler boundary
- Per-worker queue cap should be low enough to prevent “latency spiral” but high enough to keep GPUs busy.
- Proposed starting point (per worker):
  - S: 20 requests
  - M: 12 requests
  - L: 8 requests

When exceeded:
- Shed newest arrivals at scheduler boundary with reason “RUNTIME_QUEUE_FULL” (mapped to overload error).

4.2 Prefill/decode shed points
- Prefer to shed before prefill when possible (wasted compute is lower).
- For streaming, once a stream has begun:
  - strongly prefer finishing decode unless mem_pressure is critical.
  - if must shed mid-stream, return a consistent disconnect reason code in logs/traces (customer will see disconnect; support needs to interpret).

4.3 Memory pressure
- runtime_mem_pressure thresholds:
  - WARN: > 0.75 (emit warning + start rate shaping)
  - SHED: > 0.85 (shed at admission)
  - CRITICAL: > 0.93 (shed aggressively; consider forcing breaker OPEN; prevent OOM)

---

5) Per-region tuning notes (observed differences)
This section is intentionally qualitative; we should keep it grounded in dashboard panels and canary data.

5.1 us-east
- Biggest burst profile; most customer traffic; tends to hit queue issues before raw util looks “high”.
- Adjustment proposal:
  - Lower queue-based open trigger: queue_depth > 0.9 * Q_max for 30s (instead of Q_max)
  - Keep util trigger at 0.92 but shorten sustain to 45s.
- Retry-After default: 2s is reasonable (recovery tends to be fast once bursts subside).

5.2 us-west
- More variable capacity (more frequent pool resizing); util is a better predictor than queue depth.
- Adjustment proposal:
  - Keep queue trigger at Q_max/30s.
  - Util open trigger: 0.90 for 60s (slightly earlier), close util: 0.78.

5.3 eu-central
- Customer timeouts often lower (strict clients). Tail latency sensitivity is higher.
- Adjustment proposal:
  - queue_wait_p99 open threshold: 1.0s for 60s (instead of 1.25s/90s)
  - Close thresholds unchanged but extend min_open_duration to 150s to reduce oscillation.
- Retry-After: 3s (we saw longer recovery during peak EU business hours).

5.4 ap-southeast
- Smaller pools; higher variance. Risk is flapping if thresholds are too tight.
- Adjustment proposal:
  - Raise min_open_duration to 180s.
  - Use util sustain 90s (avoid opening on short spikes).
  - Half-open probe fraction cap at 1% (do not allow 5% bursts).

---

6) Dedicated alignment (notes; not final)
- Dedicated customers expect predictability. Shedding should be rare and tied to explicit contract limits (capacity) or misconfiguration.
- For Dedicated pools:
  - Prefer autoscaling + explicit “capacity exceeded” error semantics when the customer exceeds reserved throughput.
  - Breaker OPEN should likely be per-customer pool, not per shared tier.
- Action: sync with Lauren Bishop + Dedicated SRE/PM on whether we use 429 vs 503 for “reserved capacity exceeded”. (Tracked in ENG-4837.)

---

7) Observability requirements / dashboard mapping
We should be able to answer, within 2 minutes during an event:
- Which layer is shedding (gateway vs routing vs runtime)?
- Why (util, queue, mem pressure, control-plane protection)?
- How long until recovery (cooldown / trend)?

Minimum metrics to validate this doc in prod (see standard metrics doc + dashboard spec):
- breaker_state{region, model_group, tier}
- breaker_transition_total{from,to,region,model_group,tier,reason}
- shed_total{layer,reason,region,model_group,tier}
- shed_rate (derived) + admitted_rate
- gpu_pool_util{region,model_group}
- queue_depth{region,model_group}
- queue_wait_p99
- ttft_p99 (streaming)
- e2e_latency_p99 (non-streaming)
- runtime_mem_pressure

Cardinality note
- Do NOT label by raw model name and customer_id at the same time.
- Prefer model_group and tier; sample traces for high-cardinality breakdown.

---

8) Open questions / TODOs
1) Normalize Q_max by provisioned concurrency
- Current Q_max numbers are “reasonable for current pool sizes” but will drift.
- Proposal: define Q_max = k * target_concurrency where k is model_class-specific.

2) Streaming-specific thresholds
- TTFT is the customer pain metric; should TTFT drive breaker open directly for streaming routes?
- Potential: open if ttft_p99 > 2.0s for 60s on streaming routes.

3) Retry-After values
- We’re currently proposing static defaults by reason; we might do dynamic based on observed drain time (queue slope).
- Risk: oscillation and confusing client behavior if Retry-After changes too frequently.

4) Interaction with client retry storms
- Need to ensure SDKs default to exponential backoff with jitter and respect Retry-After.
- Track: ENG-4836 + docs updates.

5) Control plane protection
- When routing itself is degraded, we should shed earlier at gateway to keep control plane alive.
- Need a clean “routing degraded” signal surfaced to gateway.

---

9) Proposed next steps
- SRE (Christine/Rafael): propose final v0 defaults for us-east canary (2 models, all tiers) and publish to config schema draft.
- Observability (Aisha): ensure dashboards show breaker transitions + shed reasons clearly; validate alert windows don’t page on expected shedding.
- Platform/Routing (Mina/Ravi): validate that util/queue signals are stable enough and not delayed >30s under load.
- Run a structured game day with step-function traffic + long-prompt spikes; record if breaker opens within 90s and closes within 5–10 min post-spike.

Appendix A: Proposed defaults (copy/paste summary)
- OPEN triggers:
  - gpu_pool_util > 0.92 for 60s
  - queue_depth > Q_max for 30s (Q_max: S=200, M=120, L=60)
  - queue_wait_p99 > 1.25s for 90s
  - runtime_mem_pressure > 0.85 for 30s
- Close (OPEN → HALF_OPEN):
  - min_open 120s
  - util < 0.80 for 120s
  - queue_depth < 0.5*Q_max for 120s
  - mem_pressure < 0.70 for 120s
- HALF_OPEN probes:
  - cap: S=2 rps, M=1 rps, L=0.5 rps or 1% traffic (max 5%)
  - close to CLOSED if probe_success >= 0.98 over 2 min + p99 under targets

(End)
